This helicase is subsequently targeted by Protoxylocarpin E, a compound that may modulate cellular functions through its interaction with the helicase. The final step in this pathway involves Protoxylocarpin E interacting with Tankyrase-2, indicating a possible mechanism by which the compound influences the target enzyme. The integration of these interactions implies that Npc151898 may act as a modulator of Tankyrase-2 through the activation or inhibition of the Werner syndrome ATP-dependent helicase. The evidence supports a mechanistic link, though the exact nature of Npc151898's role in this pathway remains to be fully elucidated.
